We have the following dataset: 

```{r}
#Insert data
value<-c(42, 52, 48, 58, 32, 45, 22, 35, 28, 46)
nbooks<-c(4, 5, 4, 3, 2, 4, 1, 2, 2, 4)
sex<-factor( c(1,1,2,1,2,2,2,1,1,1), labels=c('Male', 'Female') )
income<-factor(c(1,3,5,2,2,4,1,4,4,5))
levels(income)<-c('Very low', 'Low', 'Medium', 'High', 'Very High')
income<-as.ordered(income)
#Create dataframe 
data <- data.frame(value, nbooks, sex, income)
data
```

If we don't want to print the code, we can use the argument "echo=FALSE". 
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Insert data
value<-c(42, 52, 48, 58, 32, 45, 22, 35, 28, 46)
nbooks<-c(4, 5, 4, 3, 2, 4, 1, 2, 2, 4)
sex<-factor( c(1,1,2,1,2,2,2,1,1,1), labels=c('Male', 'Female') )
income<-factor(c(1,3,5,2,2,4,1,4,4,5))
levels(income)<-c('Very low', 'Low', 'Medium', 'High', 'Very High')
income<-as.ordered(income)
data <- data.frame(value, nbooks, sex, income)
data
```


*Descriptive statistics*<br>
**Quantitative variables** <br>
Type of variables 
```{r, echo=FALSE}
str(data)
types<-sapply(data,class)
num<-which(types=="numeric")
data_num<-data[,num]
```
Basic descriptive statistics 
```{r, echo=FALSE}
sapply(data_num,summary)
```

*Plots of quantitative variables*
```{r, echo=FALSE}
histog<-function(data){
return(hist(data))
}

boxpl<-function(data){
return(boxplot(data))
}

par(mfrow=c(2,2))
sapply(data_num,histog)
sapply(data_num,boxpl)
```
**Qualitative variables**
```{r,echo=FALSE}
cat<-which(types!="numeric")
data_cat<-data[,cat]
sapply(data_cat,table)
sapply(data_cat,function(x)prop.table(table(x)))

```
Mean value and nbooks for men 


```{r, echo=FALSE}
data_male<-data[data$sex=="Male",1:2]
sapply(data_male,mean)
mean(data$value[data$sex=="Male"])
```

Frequency table of income for women

```{r, echo=FALSE}
data_fem<-data$income[data$sex=="Female"]
prop.table(table(data_fem))
table(data_fem)/length(data_fem)
#pay attention, different percentages
table(data$income[data$sex=="Female"])/nrow(data)
```

Add a new variable that indicates whether someone has or not children.
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Simulate 10 values from bernoulli with p=0.6. 
#Add these values in a new column of dataset 2 with the name "Indication"
sim<-rbinom(10,1,0.6)
data$Indication<-sim
data
```
